source.title: Efficient-Adam: Communication-Efficient Distributed Adam
source.authors: Cong-Liang Chen; Li Shen; Wei Liu; Z. Luo

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares adaptive and SGD-based optimizers on held-out classification performance, using its own distributed optimization recipes and reporting qualitative comparisons rather than a direct generalization-gap analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on CIFAR100 and IMDB. Other experiments on quantization, error feedback, and convergence do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out accuracy comparisons between Adam-based and momentum-SGD-based methods in a distributed, quantized training setting. These bear on V4, although communication schemes and optimization progress complicate attribution to optimizer choice.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that Efficient-Adam reduces communication while retaining effective optimization and task performance. They establish convergence and communication-complexity guarantees, report comparable CIFAR100 performance to Zheng's method, and report Adam-based methods outperforming SGD-based methods on IMDB. They leave distributed linear speedup unestablished.
record.recipe_differences: Distributed Adam and SGD-based methods with communication quantization/error feedback are compared; these are not the optimizer comparison recipes specified in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported direction differs by dataset: SGD-based methods are favored on CIFAR100, while Adam-based methods are favored on IMDB.
record.problems: The optimizer comparisons are shown in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The experiments use specific distributed algorithms and selected learning rates; they do not directly quantify the training–test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No separately described held-out optimizer comparison results were omitted. Additional figure curves for individual quantization and error-feedback variants are not separately extracted because the text does not describe each curve's test-accuracy outcome.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; word-level language modeling; and whether held-out differences persist at matched training performance.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. CIFAR100 learning rates were selected using test accuracy, weakening interpretation as independently evaluated held-out performance. Figures are represented only by captions in the supplied text, so numerical gaps and individual curve rankings cannot be verified. The authors' general explanation favoring SGD for images cites Wilson et al.; the narrower communication-budget comparison is their own result. IMDB's reversal qualifies an 'often' claim rather than refuting it universally.

versions.untested_parts: No broad optimizer sweep, language-model benchmark, equal-training-performance generalization-gap analysis, or extensive tuning comparison.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.size_stated: 17 convolutional layers and one fully-connected layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam-based distributed algorithms; test accuracy compared with SGD-based methods.
rows.note: Text says SGD-based methods are more suitable for image classification; Zheng et al. achieves the best result and the proposed Adam method is similar to it. Exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The text reports Efficient-Adam performing similarly to Zheng's momentum SGD, with Zheng best when measured against communication bits. This supports at most a limited adaptive-method disadvantage. Separate comparisons at matched iterations from comparisons at matched communication budgets; exact accuracies are unavailable.
